text: {"score":3,"justification":"The summary is mostly grounded: the headline numbers (18.3% vs 6.7%, z 2.52, risk score 7.04, 22 documented claims, 2 of 13 notes) match the card, and it is cautious and leans inconclusive. But it has several errors and inconsistencies. The headline says 99215 runs above peers in every complexity band, yet the 0-condition band is 0.01 vs 0.019, which is below. The rationale says roughly double the all-provider rate in each band from 1 to 5+, but 5+ is 0.48 vs 0.254 (about 1.9x), 1 is about 2.1x, 3 is 1.8x, and 4 is 2.6x, so 'roughly double' is loose. The claim that excess is concentrated among 4+ conditions rests on the example claims and the band shares, which is partly supportable, but 'steepest excess in sicker patients' is only partly right in relative terms. The text also says C0011574 has 'no chronic conditions' correctly, but the cited claim list contains only C0010444 and C0010560, while other claim IDs appear in the text without being cited. Next steps are generic and do not name the targeted charts that the rationale recommends, and 'Re-screen' is weak. It does not mention that the 2 of 13 no-lab notes are weak.","problems":["Headline 'above peers in every complexity band' is contradicted by the 0-condition band (1% vs 1.9%).","'Roughly double within each band from 1 to 5+' is imprecise; ratios range from about 1.8x to 2.6x.","Claim IDs C0010436, C0011388, C0011100, C0011574 and C0011079 appear in the text but are not in cited_claim_ids; the cited examples are only low-complexity ones and support none of the high-complexity points.","Next steps are generic and do not match the targeted chart request in the rationale (low-complexity 99215 claims, 4+ condition sample).","Awkward grammar ('Of 1 documented 99215 claims') and 8% low-complexity share is described without a comparison to peers.","The 99215 flag from the number check is just the CPT code, so it is not a real problem."]}
